title: Equivariant lisse extension on the full parameter-root tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing $E$ with the extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for every profinite set $P$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories and total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme with a finite reduced strict normal crossings divisor $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Put $W=Y\setminus D$, and let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization the pullback of $L$ to the complement becomes constant after adjoining compatible roots of all boundary parameters of all positive orders prime to $p$; strict henselization is [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Fix $I\subseteq A$ and the reduced stratum $S_I=(\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i)\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$.
There are affine etale charts $V\to Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$ with equations $t_i$ for $D_i$, affine pro-etale maps $U_\alpha\to V$, and $S_\alpha=U_\alpha\times_Y S_I$, such that the $S_\alpha\to S_I$ cover in the pro-etale topology. Put
$$T_\alpha=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}_{U_\alpha}\bigl(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}[x_i]_{i\in I}/(x_i^n-t_i)_{i\in I}\bigr),\qquad T_\alpha^\circ=T_\alpha\times_YW.$$
Transitions are the power maps for divisibility. There are compatible primitive roots of unity on $U_\alpha$ of all orders prime to $p$, identifying the deck group with $G_I=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^I$. The map $T_\alpha^\circ\to U_\alpha^\circ=U_\alpha\times_YW$ is a pro-etale cover and a $G_I$-torsor: $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ identifies $T_\alpha^\circ[G_I]$ with $T_\alpha^\circ\times_{U_\alpha^\circ}T_\alpha^\circ$, where profinite products mean inverse limits of finite disjoint unions [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. There is a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,T_\alpha}$-module $\widetilde L_\alpha$ with continuous $G_I$-equivariant structure whose restriction to $T_\alpha^\circ$ is the actual deck-equivariant pullback of $L$. The map $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to T_\alpha$ sets every root to zero. For some finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $M_\alpha$ there is a $G_I$-equivariant identification
$$i_\alpha^*\widetilde L_\alpha\cong p_{S_\alpha}^*(P\mapsto C(P,M_\alpha)),$$
whose action is induced by a continuous $E$-linear representation $G_I\to\operatorname{GL}_E(M_\alpha)$. The constructions restrict along refinements of this family. For $I=\varnothing$ the root tower and group are the identity and the trivial group, and this is a pro-etale trivialization of $L$. No assertion about higher direct images is included.

proof.text: Apply the residual-chart lemma to $(Y,D,I)$ and retain one member $V,U,S_U,T,T^\circ$. It supplies affine charts, the pro-etale cover of the entire stratum, compatible primitive roots, and the actual power-transition tower. These choices depend on the pair, not on a pointwise trivialization of $L$. For $S_I=\varnothing$ take the empty family. Below work on a nonempty member; $U^\circ$ and $T^\circ$ are connected and qcqs.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input.

proof.text: Let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\varpi$. The finite-type Noetherian lemma applies to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal); its open-subscheme version applies to $W$. Regularity makes $W$ normal; separation is inherited from $Y$. Identify internal modules with section-ring module sheaves and pulled-back $C(-,E)$ with continuous-function coefficients. The integral reduction equivalence identifies the coefficient rings with $B_W=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_W$ and $B_W[1/\varpi]$. The normal completed integral-model theorem gives a lisse integral model $N$ with $N[1/\varpi]\cong L$. Thus $F_n=N/\varpi^nN$ is a normalized tower of finite locally free discrete-coefficient sheaves. Restrict $N,F_n$ to the open part of any chart.

source.place: Lemmas 6.8.2 and 7.4.10; Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4); integral lattice on a normal scheme

proof.text: At a geometric boundary point pull $N$ to its punctured strict-local full root tower $Z$. This $Z$ is connected and qcqs by the chart lemma's strict-local assertion. Tameness makes its rationalization constant, say $E_Z^d$. The lattice-class sheaf lemma identifies the class of $(N|_Z,E_Z\otimes N|_Z\cong E_Z^d)$ with a section of the constant discrete sheaf $\operatorname{GL}_d(E)/\operatorname{GL}_d(A)$. The continuous-function realization for a discrete space identifies that section with a continuous map from $|Z|$ into this discrete set. Connectedness makes it constant, with value the coset of a matrix $h$. By the lemma's embedded-image normalization the integral module is $hA_Z^d$, isomorphic to $A_Z^d$. Exact pullback and the integral coefficient reduction formula identify the pulled-back $F_n$ with $(A/\varpi^n)_Z^d$. Every $F_n$ therefore satisfies the finite tame hypothesis, also where fewer boundary branches vanish. Integral tameness has been deduced from rational tameness.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), lattice-class sheaf, and Lemma 4.2.12; finite-E coefficients only

proof.text: Apply finite tame-fibre classification to the restrictions of all $F_n$ on this chart. The same $U$ works for every $n$: it was formed from all finite residual covers. This gives finite free $A/\varpi^n$-modules $Q_n$ with continuous $G_I$-action, compatible quotient transitions, and natural identifications $F_n|_{T^\circ}\cong\underline{Q_n}$. Its product and coefficient compatibilities give the linear operations and reduction isomorphisms. The descent action is exactly the action on $Q_n$, not an action selected independently at the boundary. The finite-local-system assertion here is on the pro-etale site, as stated in that lemma.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input.

proof.text: Set $Q=\varprojlim_nQ_n$ and $M=E\otimes_AQ$. Adic finite-module reconstruction gives $Q/\varpi^nQ\cong Q_n$, finite generation, completeness and the inverse-limit topology. It is finite free: choose a basis of $Q_1$ and lift it successively through $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. Each lifted basis is a basis over $A/\varpi^{n+1}$, since its change-of-basis determinant is a unit modulo $\varpi$. These choices give compatible $Q_n\cong(A/\varpi^n)^d$, hence $Q\cong A^d$. Define $g(q_n)_n=(gq_n)_n$. This action is jointly continuous because each composite $G_I\times Q\to Q_n$ is continuous. In a basis its matrix entries are inverse limits of continuous finite-valued entries; inverse matrices come from $g^{-1}$. Extension of scalars gives a continuous homomorphism $\rho:G_I\to\operatorname{GL}_E(M)$. No finite-image claim is needed.

Identify the actual torsor. At order $n$, root rotations send $x_i$ to $\zeta_n^{a_i}x_i$. On the punctured locus every $x_i$ is a unit. For two root tuples over the same base the ratios $y_i/x_i$ have $n$th power one. The factorization $z^n-1=\prod_{a\bmod n}(z-\zeta_n^a)$ has pairwise comaximal factors, since distinct-root differences are units. Its Chinese-remainder idempotents decompose the base uniquely into pieces on which each ratio is one $\zeta_n^{a_i}$. This gives the scheme isomorphism $T_n^\circ[(\mathbf Z/n)^I]\cong T_n^\circ\times_{U^\circ}T_n^\circ$, $(x,a)\mapsto(x,\zeta_n^ax)$. Power transitions send $a$ to its residue and preserve this formula. Taking affine inverse limits gives $T^\circ[G_I]\cong T^\circ\times_{U^\circ}T^\circ$. Here $\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}(\mathbf Z/n)^I=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^I$ by compatible Chinese-remainder decomposition into prime powers. The covering assertion was supplied by the chart lemma.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input.

proof.text: The composite $T^\circ\to W$ is a pro-etale object. The coefficient-section localization lemma identifies its actual inverse image with slice restriction. Restriction to a slice preserves all limits, since limits of sheaves are computed objectwise. Apply it to $N\cong\varprojlim_nF_n$. The natural finite-level identifications in step 4 and compatible bases in step 5 identify this restricted limit with $\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_{T^\circ}^d\cong A_{T^\circ}^d$, by the coefficient reduction equivalence and its actual projection maps. Inverting $\varpi$ gives $L|_{T^\circ}\cong p_{T^\circ}^*C(-,M)$, since $C(P,M)=C(P,E)^d$ in the chosen basis. Every projection identifies deck descent with $\rho_n$, so their limit identifies it with $\rho$ on $M$. Equality of actions is tested by the limit projections before localization.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Proposition 6.8.4(1); inverse limits after slice restriction

proof.text: Define on all of $T$ the module $\widetilde L=p_T^*C(-,M)$. In the chosen basis it is $C_{E,T}^d$, hence finite-rank lisse. Give it the continuous equivariant structure induced by $G_I\times M\to M$ and root rotations on $T$. The cocycle identity is $\rho(gh)=\rho(g)\rho(h)$. Step 7 identifies its restriction, with this action, with the actual deck-equivariant pullback of $L$. Define $i:S_U\to T$ by $H_\infty\to H/JH$ taking every root variable to zero: all defining and transition equations map to zero. Root rotations fix $i$. Composition of pullback from the point gives $i^*\widetilde L\cong p_{S_U}^*C(-,M)$ with exactly the same representation $\rho$. This constructs the extension and its specified boundary action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input.

proof.text: Pointed refinement maps of the charts and finite-fibre classification give maps of rings, finite fibres and actions commuting with every quotient projection. The inverse-limit universal property makes the representation and step 7's identification commute with these maps. Pullback of the finite basis and the matrix formula $v\mapsto\rho(g)v$ identify step 8's constant extension and its boundary restriction under refinement. Changing compatible bases conjugates every $\rho_n$ by the corresponding compatible matrices, hence gives the conjugate representation and an isomorphic extension. Restriction compatibility thus holds for these choices.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input.

proof.text: For $I=\varnothing$ all root rings equal $H$ and $G_I=1$. Finite classification gives constant $F_n$ on $U$, and steps 5 and 7 reconstruct a constant $L|_U$. Set $T=U$, $i=\mathrm{id}_U$ and use this trivialization. Rank zero gives $Q_n=Q=M=\widetilde L=0$. Ranks may vary between the connected charts because $M$ is chosen per chart. Empty boundary and empty whole scheme are included.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Separate residual-neighborhood geometry and normalized finite tame-cover classification. Reuse normal integral models and lattice-class rigidity. Construct the inverse-limit inertia representation, actual torsor, constant equivariant extension, boundary restriction and refinements explicitly. Two statement-only nodes, no Mathlib leaves.
blueprint: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the tame-boundary Kummer calculation, specifically the equivariant lisse extension input. Steps 1–4 expose geometric and coefficient inputs; steps 5–10 construct the equivariant extension rather than citing an infinite-coefficient restatement.

tool_uses.why: Step 2 applies finite-type permanence to Y over the Noetherian field k. This is a scheme-theoretic prerequisite for integral lattices, not a replacement of the open-direct-image route; the unit contains no such permanence statement.
Step 2 passes Noetherianity from Y to its open W, to check the integral-model hypotheses. This general topological permanence input is not supplied by the unit.
Step 2 uses clause (1), regular implies normal, on W. The direct-image unit does not prove normality of regular schemes.

Step 2 identifies the finite-E pulled-back condensed coefficients with the section-ring continuous-function coefficients required by the integral-model theorem. The identification is coefficient infrastructure, not an alternate finiteness argument.
Steps 2, 3 and 7 use the explicit coefficient ring identifications and the natural inverse-limit/reduction equivalence. The unit does not construct normalized integral coefficient towers.
Step 2 takes an abstract integral model on normal Noetherian separated W, with ell invertible. No embedding is inferred from this theorem. The unit does not prove the existence of integral models.

Step 3 uses the actual lattice-class sheaf GL_d(E)/GL_d(A), including its embedded-image normalization. This generic lattice rigidity input converts the assumed rational tameness to finite-reduction tameness; it does not assert the desired extension.

Step 3 uses exact coefficient pullback to identify reductions after restriction to a strict-local root tower. This is inverse-image infrastructure, not the direct-image finiteness theorem being studied.
Step 5 uses clause (1) to reconstruct finite modules from normalized finite quotients, with their adic topology. The unit does not contain this algebraic reconstruction theorem.
Step 7 uses the actual identification of pro-etale inverse image with slice restriction so that limits can be restricted objectwise. The unit does not supply that site-localization identification.

B^h is Noetherian (0AGV) and an ind-étale colimit over regular B, so it is regular, and connected because (B^h,JB^h) is henselian with B/J connected. The finite étale lifts with connected special fibre are normal domains, so H is a domain and U° is connected. H_n is regular at the boundary because t_i are regular parameters, and Spec H_n is connected because the pair is henselian with special fibre (H/JH)[x]/x^n. Primitive ζ_n come from μ_n covers of S_V and Hensel, and their differences are units since ∏(1−ζ^c)=n. (2) lem-sfb-snc-tame-finite-fibre-classification is the Grothendieck–Murre tame π1 over a henselian SNC neighbourhood with simply connected residual stratum. It holds by Abhyankar at strict-local points, then purity on regular H_n, then 09ZS splitting over S_U. I tested both on one branch of A^1 at 0 (strictly henselian DVR, tame π1=Ẑ'(1)), on two branches at the origin of A^2, and on r=0, rank 0 and an empty stratum. The finite node excludes infinite coefficients and limits, so it does not restate the item (D1/D2). None of the 8 candidate duplicates I checked (per-snc-root-punctured-torsor-splitting, per-snc-parameter-root-quotient, sbc-strict-hensel-root-finite-etale-model, root-tower-lisse-morphism-extension, root-tower-boundary-acyclicity, pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover, dl-a1-henselian-global-inertia-comparison, pbc henselization family) states either node. Step 3: the punctured strict-local tower Z is a connected qcqs pro-étale object of W, the lattice sheaf is the constant GL_d(E)/GL_d(A), and the totally-disconnected realization gives C(π0 Z,S)=S, so N|_Z≅A^d and integral tameness follows from rational tameness. Step 4: one U serves all n, and the reduction clause gives Q_{n+1}/ϖ^n≅Q_n. Step 5: the hypotheses of pod-adic-limit (1) are met, basis lifting works, and ρ is continuous. Step 6: the comaximal CRT argument is a correct elementary step. Step 7: slice restriction preserves limits, so N≅lim F_n gives L|_{T°}≅E^d with descent ρ. Steps 8–10: the root-to-zero map preserves the equations since t_i∈J, and the I=∅, rank-0 and empty cases are handled. BATCH 5: def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary is a general definition. lem-a1-normal-completed-integral-model reaches lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice, which is generic stable-lattice theory. lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules is pure O_E commutative algebra. None is a step of Poincaré duality or the trace formula, so all three are accepted. I accept the 10 generic tool_uses (listed in review.md).
